summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -3 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +6.1%; weakest: Lean hogs -18.4%. Key releases ahead: US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.98% (-26 bp in a month), 2-year 4.73% (-7 bp); 2s10s curve +25 bp (-19 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 102.91 (+0.3% in a month, +4.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.560 (+11.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.662 (-0.4%); USD/MXN 18.62 (+1.1%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.1% in a month (+11.7% YTD); VIX 17.5. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 87.04 $/bbl (-6.3% in a month), Brent 93.13, ULSD 4.232 $/gal (-7.7%), natural gas 3.25 (-7.2%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -6.8% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.1%, Hang Seng +0.2%, yuan +0.4% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -7.8% in a month; gold -4.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
